reason: Attacked and it held. I downloaded Project Gutenberg 3800, the Elwes translation, and read the last page of Part V myself: PROP. XLII stands at line 9670, its Note follows, and at lines 9710 to 9717 the four sentences run exactly as proposed, ending immediately before the line End of the Ethics by Benedict de Spinoza. Word for word and comma for comma, including Needs must it be hard with no indeed, great labour with the British spelling, the question mark after neglected, and But all things excellent are as difficult as they are rare rather than the common variant But all noble things. The locator is right: Part V, Proposition XLII, Note, and it genuinely is the close of the work, so the closing-line fame test is met and not merely asserted. Elwes 1883 is the right year for the Bohn Chief Works translation, and naming the man Baruch Spinoza where that edition prints Benedict de Spinoza is the ordinary English form, not a change of wording. The source line is 107 characters, leads with the name, carries no dash and no straight quote; the quotation ends in a full stop; the tag Philosophy is the form of the work. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, Spinoza at 0 of 3, not banned. In scope, publishable, and on the month theme of a hard way that is nevertheless there to be walked. Nothing to break.
